text: This case separates three questions: whether performance is substantial, which defects are compensable, and how each defect should be valued. It links the conditions doctrine in Jacob & Youngs to the competing damages measures in Groves and Peevyhouse.
sourceSummary: A substantially performing homebuilder could recover the unpaid price subject to appropriate defect deductions; replacing a misplaced interior wall was too wasteful when the wall caused no loss in market value.
basis: Synthesis of the cited assigned excerpt.
